# A. Smallest Primitive Root

## How to find it

Factor `p-1` and reject a candidate if removing any distinct prime factor from the exponent makes it one.

## Correctness

The order divides `p-1`; it is proper exactly when it divides `(p-1)/q` for some prime divisor `q`.

## Complexity

Factorization plus `O(number tested * omega(p-1) log p)`.

# C. General Discrete Log

## How to find it

Strip common gcd factors until modular inverses become legal, then run BSGS on the adjusted equation.

## Correctness

Each stripping step is necessary and equivalent after accounting for its forced base factor; the final coprime equation is handled exhaustively by BSGS.

## Complexity

`O(log m + sqrt(m))` expected time and `O(sqrt(m))` memory.

# D. Modular Square Roots

## How to find it

Use Euler classification, split `p-1=q*2^s`, and cancel the two-power discrepancy with a known nonresidue.

## Correctness

Tonelli--Shanks maintains `x squared = a*t` and moves `t` into successively smaller two-power subgroups until `t=1`.

## Complexity

`O(log squared p)` modular operations.
